provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for winter: 4 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 薄霜 usu-shimo (#E7EAED), then 冬杉 fuyu-sugi (#1C3E28), then 冬影 fuyu-kage (#494A66), then 霜夜 shimo-yo (#15202F). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 65.6, 28.4, 16.0 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: Frost over evergreen, read outermost first: a thin-frost white (薄霜) over a winter cedar green (冬杉), then a violet winter shadow (冬影), and a frost-night blue-black (霜夜) as the innermost edge. The green is the only chromatic layer, which is how an evergreen reads in winter — the one colour left. The name is ours (霜杉, "Frosted Cedar"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
